title: People Ops - Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook (2026)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook documents Redwood Inference's standard processes for hiring, new-employee onboarding, and the performance & feedback cycle. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and people managers responsible for engineering and cross-functional teams. The document contains checklists, templates, role ownership, timing expectations, and escalation paths.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time employees (FTEs) and full-time equivalent contractors hired through Redwood recruiting channels.
- Does not replace role-specific technical rubrics in team pages; this playbook references those rubrics and provides company-level requirements.

Hiring process: high-level flow

1) Requisition & Approval
   - Manager creates a role requisition in Greenhouse following the team staffing plan and tags People Ops as approver. Required fields: role summary, seniority, hiring manager, expected band, budget code, and target hire date.
   - People Ops signs off on headcount, compensation band range, and required compliance checks within 3 business days.

2) Sourcing & Screen
   - Recruiter sources candidates and runs an initial phone screen (30 min) to validate role fit and basics (work authorization, salary expectations, notice period).
   - Recruiter updates candidate scorecard in Greenhouse and routes to hiring manager for next steps.

3) Interview Loop
   - Standard on-site (virtual) loop for engineering roles: Recruiter screen -> Hiring Manager / Functional interview -> System design or technical assessment -> Culture / Values interview -> Bar raiser (if applicable) -> Compensation & calibration debrief.
   - Interview length: 60-90 minutes each; target total candidate time 3-4 hours.
   - Interviewers must use the standard scorecard rubric (1-4 scale) and submit feedback within 48 hours. Hiring manager collects feedback and arranges calibration if scores are mixed.

Interview rubric (company-level requirements)

| Dimension | 1 (Below) | 2 (Meets) | 3 (Strong) | 4 (Exceptional) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Technical skills | Unable to reason about components, major gaps | Solid implementation skills for role at level | Strong design and tradeoff reasoning | Inventive solutions, mentors others |
| System design / architecture | Not adequate for scope | Covers basic patterns and scaling | Designs for reliability, cost, and failure modes | Leads complex architecture tradeoffs |
| Ownership & communication | Poor communicator, unclear accountability | Clear and responsive | Proactive owner, strong cross-team communication | Inspires and simplifies complex work |
| Culture & values | Values mismatch or ethics concerns | Aligns with Redwood values | Exemplifies values consistently | Role model and mentor for values |

Minimum pass rule: No dimension should be rated 1; overall average >=2.5 for standard hires. Senior and leadership roles require at least one 4 and no 1s.

Offer & negotiation

- People Ops prepares the offer packet (compensation summary, equity guidance, benefits summary, expected start date, and basic relocation/remote policy).
- Manager approves final offer. Offers should be extended within 5 business days of final decision.
- Recruiter manages negotiation; exceptions (above-band offers, sign-on > 2 months equivalent, or unusual equity grants) routed to Head of People Ops and Finance for approval.

Onboarding: pre-start & first 90 days

Pre-start (1-2 weeks before start) checklist
- Recruiter sends welcome packet and first-day logistics (ID, laptop allocation form, parking/remote setup).
- People Ops creates account provisioning ticket to Eng Infra with required entitlements and target completion 48 hours before start.
- Manager prepares first-week plan including 1:1 schedule, onboarding buddy assignment, and project-oriented reading list.

First week (Day 0-5)
- Day 0: HR orientation (company mission, values, benefits, payroll, code of conduct).
- Day 1: Manager 30-60 min welcome, team intro, and setup check. Assign onboarding checklist in Confluence.
- Technical setup: access to repos, Slack, Jira, SSO, dev machines. Escalation to Eng Infra if any access missing by end of Day 1.
- Buddy program: buddy assigned for first 30 days for practical questions and social introductions.

First 30 days (Month 1) - focus: context & contribution
- Goal: ship a small, scoped task with a mentor.
- Weekly 1:1s between manager and new hire with documented agenda in Workday/Confluence.
- Learning checkpoints: codebase overview, architecture readme, security checklist, and test runbook.

60-90 days - focus: ownership & impact
- New hire presents a 30/60 day summary to manager and team.
- Manager and People Ops complete a calibration touchpoint to confirm role level, any support needs, and performance expectations.
- If performance concerns exist, manager should initiate a Development Plan (see section below).

Performance & feedback cycles

Quarterly cycle (standard for all teams)
- Timeline: goal-setting at start of quarter, mid-quarter check-in, and end-of-quarter review. People Ops publishes the quarterly calendar each year.
- Managers are responsible for documenting goals (OKRs / SMART goals) and linking them to team roadmap items.
- Mid-quarter check-in: informal written note in the employee's profile and a 1:1 conversation.
- End-of-quarter review: manager submits written performance summary and proposed rating to People Ops for calibration.

Performance ratings and calibration
- Rating bands (Descriptive): Needs Improvement, Meets Expectations, Exceeds Expectations, Exceptional. Numeric mapping 1-4 for internal grading.
- Manager assigns preliminary rating; People Ops convenes a calibration panel per department to ensure consistency and equity.
- Calibration factors include scope of impact, competency at level, growth trajectory, and business results.

Feedback best practices for managers
- Provide frequent, specific feedback: at least weekly informal feedback and monthly documented 1:1 notes.
- Use the SBI model (Situation, Behavior, Impact) for constructive feedback.
- Document strengths and development areas; set 2-3 concrete development goals per quarter.

Development Plans & performance improvement

- For employees rated 'Needs Improvement' or with recurring performance concerns, manager creates a Performance Development Plan (PDP) with People Ops.
- PDP elements: expected outcomes, measurable success criteria, resources & coaching plan, timeline (typically 60-90 days), and escalation steps.
- People Ops reviews PDP and assigns a People Ops partner to monitor progress. If insufficient improvement, follow the disciplinary and separation process defined in HR policies.

Manager responsibilities & manager onboarding

- Managers must complete Manager Essentials training within 60 days of promotion/hire: topics include legal basics, feedback & coaching, inclusive hiring, compensation conversations, and performance calibration.
- Manager checklist for new direct reports: 30/60/90 plans, role expectations doc, alignment with career ladder, and time blocked weekly for coaching.

Templates & examples (copy in Confluence)

- Interview scorecard template: link to team-specific rubrics.
- Offer letter template: standard FTE and contractor variants.
- 30/60/90 plan template: sections for goals, success metrics, stakeholders, and learning milestones.
- PDP template: clear outcomes, check-ins, and sign-off fields for manager, employee, and People Ops.

Escalations & SLAs

- Access provisioning SLA: People Ops to Eng Infra ticket <48 hours before start; escalation to Head of Eng Infra if unresolved by Day 1.
- Offer approval SLA: People Ops approval within 3 business days of requisition.
- Interview feedback SLA: interviewers must submit feedback within 48 hours. Recruiters to follow up after 72 hours.

Compliance & background checks

- All candidates offered a position are subject to background checks per local regulations. For roles with data access or security constraints, additional checks and signing of NDA and security addendums are required prior to full access.

Confidentiality & data handling

- People Ops and hiring managers must store candidate data in Greenhouse only. Do not email CVs to non-interviewers nor store candidate sensitive data in personal drives.

Ownership & contacts

- Recruiting lead: Michael Chen - recruiting@redwood.example.com
- Eng Infra (provisioning): Dev Ops team runbook (see eng-infra runbooks).

Appendix: Quick checklists (copyable)

Requisition checklist:
- Headcount approved in staffing plan
- Role description + success criteria
- Job posting drafted and SaaS posting instructions set
- Compensation band approved
- Hiring timeline and interviewers assigned

First-week manager checklist:
- 1:1 schedule for first 90 days created
- Technical mentor and buddy assigned
- Small onboarding task scoped and assigned
- Access verification completed by end of Day 1

Performance check-in checklist:
- Mid-quarter 1:1 documented
- End-of-quarter written summary submitted
- Calibration meeting attended with required artifacts

For questions or exceptions, contact People Ops.
